named_subject: a lion (round smiling face inside a spiky mane, with a long low body), lying down
action: The black lion slides in from the left edge and moves to the middle of the frame, where it stays lying down, while a grey lion on the right drifts off to the right as the view pans.
identity_gap: The face and spiky mane match the doodle closely, but the black body is drawn as a flat line with one low hump, and the doodle's two arched leg loops are mostly missing.
notes: For frames 1 to 6 the only lion is drawn in grey as scenery, so the black character is absent; in frames 7 and 8 it appears only as a stray mane fragment at the frame edge, and in frame 9 it pops in already half visible. The change that would help most is to have the black character enter as a complete drawing that slides in smoothly from the left edge over frames 7 to 9, and to keep the doodle's two leg arches on the body.
